{{Nihongo|'''Tsutomu Miyasaka'''|宮坂力|Miyasaka Tsutomu|born September 10, 1953}}, is a Japanese engineer in [[electrochemistry]] best known as the inventor of the [[perovskite solar cell]].<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite journal|last1=Kojima|first1=Akihiro|last2=Teshima|first2=Kenjiro|last3=Shirai|first3=Yasuo|last4=Miyasaka|first4=Tsutomu|title=Organometal Halide Perovskites as Visible-Light Sensitizers for Photovoltaic Cells|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|date=May 6, 2009|volume=131|issue=17|pages=6050–6051|doi=10.1021/ja809598r|pmid=19366264}}</ref>

==Education ==
Miyasaka graduated from the Applied Chemistry Department of [[Waseda University]] in March 1976. He obtained a master's degree in industrial chemistry from the [[University of Tokyo]] (UTokyo) in 1978. He was a visiting researcher at the [[University of Quebec]] in Canada in 1980 when he was study Ph.D. in synthetic chemistry at the UTokyo.<ref>{{Cite web|title=MIYASAKA Group|url=https://www.cc.toin.ac.jp/sc/miyasaka/en/about/index.html|website=TOIN University of Yokohama}}</ref>

==Career==
Miyasaka joined [[Fujifilm]] after completing his PhD in March 1981,<ref name="OplusE">[https://www.adcom-media.co.jp/remark/2016/10/25/24284/ ペロブスカイトの成功は人のつながりがなければ成し得なかった] OplusE「私の発言」 2016.10.25 アドコム・メディア</ref> he worked on the development of high-sensitivity films for photo camera films for instant cameras and the development of [[lithium-ion battery]].<ref name="OplusE"/> However, Fujifilm has discontinued development of lithium-ion battery due to "impossible to make a profit". After being recruited, he became a professor at Graduate School of Engineering at [[Toin University of Yokohama]] in 2001.<ref name="OplusE"/>

Meantime in 2004, in response to the promotion of the venture company's founding policy by the mayor of [[Yokohama City]], Miyasaka established Peccell Technologies for [[solar cell]] research and served as the representative director until 2009.<ref name="OplusE"/>

He also developed the first [[photocapacitor]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2004-11-04|title=A new type of solar cell|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/a-new-type-of-solar-cell/|access-date=2021-06-15|website=Physics World|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Miyasaka|first1=Tsutomu|last2=Murakami|first2=Takurou N.|date=2004-10-25|title=The photocapacitor: An efficient self-charging capacitor for direct storage of solar energy|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/full/10.1063/1.1810630|journal=Applied Physics Letters|volume=85|issue=17|pages=3932–3934|doi=10.1063/1.1810630|bibcode=2004ApPhL..85.3932M |issn=0003-6951|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=K|first1=Namsheer|last2=Rout|first2=Chandra Sekhar|date=2021-04-06|title=Photo-powered integrated supercapacitors: a review on recent developments, challenges and future perspectives|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2021/ta/d1ta00444a|journal=Journal of Materials Chemistry A|language=en|volume=9|issue=13|pages=8248–8278|doi=10.1039/D1TA00444A|s2cid=233559607 |issn=2050-7496|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Since 2009, Miyasaka has been working on research and development of [[perovskite solar cell]], therefore, he won the [[Clarivate Citation Laureates]] in 2017.<ref name="Clarivate">{{Cite web|title=Identifying extreme impact in research, Clarivate Analytics uses citations to forecast Nobel Prize winners|url=https://clarivate.com/news/identifying-extreme-impact-research-clarivate-analytics-uses-citations-forecast-nobel-prize-winners/|access-date=2021-06-15|website=Clarivate|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2017 Miyasaka was awarded the Hamakawa award for his contribution in photovoltaic science and technology development.<ref name="PVSEC">{{Cite web|title=Awards|url=https://www.pvsec.org/awards.html|access-date=2021-06-15|website=PVSEC|language=en}}</ref>
